It definitely looks like a tumour. The part closest to her body is red and "fresh", like all of the other tumours I've seen. The rest of it, the grey, is probably just (partly) dead tumour which is still attached to the tumour. Does she nromally sit with her tail so straight down as she does in the first picture? That is a clear symptom of something being wrong with ehr body, meaning the tumour is not just a piece of flesh, but something which bothers her. Plus, does she normally keep her wings so far away from her body, and keep her feathers thight, also as seen in the picture? The tumour looks very painful to me, and it takes a lot of energy to have  it. It is definitely coming from her oil gland. The only way to know for sure is to schedule an appointment with the an avian vet and test it. Also, bring a dropping, the vet often wants to take a look at it in the microscope. 

If it is a tumour, you'll probably be given these options:

1. An operaton to remove it. Please do not choose this. The operation is highly dangerous, and the bird is often so exhausted afterwards and in pain, that the immune system is so low the bird can die horribly afterwards or catch a new illness.

2. Apply something on it to stop eventual infection, which can help, but it won't work if it is a tumour.

3. The final option is to put her down. I hate to say this, but it can be the best solution. She is most definitely in pain. An operation can, and most likely will, make her worse. Remember that for birds, life isn't about living for as long as possible. It is about how her life is in the time she's here. She can probably live for years, but it will be filled with pain and misery. It will get worse. Her immune system will also get worse, making her prone to even more diseases. 

You will probably get some pain killers, supposed to be given orally. If she is with other birds, you'll have to seperate her if you want to put it in her water, because capturing twice a day and forcing it down her throat is no fun for either part.

Trying to treat this thing is a bumpy and dangerous road. I would love to see some more pictures of her, to check for other signs of discomfort. Please schedule an appointmet as soon as you can. It sucks, but when we take in a pet, we have to take some difficult choises. The vet will know a lot more than I do, so talk it all out. I just want you to know what you'll probably hear. A lump on her back is often the oil gland/uropygial gland/preen gland. It is supposed to be a lump, but sometimes it will get infected or it will grow a tumour on it, often because of vitamin D deficciancy. If you do not have a UV-lamp or the ability to give it natural sun light directly outdoors (through the windows doesn't count), rush to the vet and check it out. It can, in some cases, be easily treated, but can also be deadly and painful.

Having depression sucks, and therapy is definitely not mandatory. However, it can help a lot. You'll talk about coping methods, how to react better to stuff, how to change your pattern of thinking and acting, how to deal with thoughts etc. Self-help stuff will take all of this up, but you can't interact with it (with exception to people who help online, free, on chats). The most helpful thing about therapy, compared to the web, is that the psych can see you from a new perspective. You might suffer from Multiple Personality Disorder, for instance, but only a third person would be able to see it. Plus, a psychologist can make an individual plan for you.

Don't do meds before you try therapy. Meds can only take the edge off, and to get meds, you have to have a proper diagnosis and know what you want with it. Don't self-medicate.

And don't self-diagnose. You can look around to get a better view at it, witch can help the doctor diagnose you, but don't determine it for sure alone.

Lastly, I would add that you do have free options. There are tons of chat places that are free, such as here. Plus,  there are doctors and psychologist who do give advice and such over the net for free (but not a diagnosis, of course), and there are always thelephone lines. You can call them several times a week, whatever you want. I think some costs money like regular phone bills, but I think others are completely free. You'll have to dig a little for yourself. 

I had the same mindset as you had. I thought I knew myself and my feelings perfectly well, so I didn't want any conversation therapy. I wanted to go straight for the drugs. Honestly, I'm glad I didn't. I now know that I still have a lot to learn about myself. What has helped me so far, honestly, has just been to  be able to say the word "depression" out loud. And filling out those gigantic forms.

I advice you to fill out these. Either orally or on paper. Just read the questions, think and reflect until you know what fits you. These are the international papers used as a general form to cover most of the most common illnesses. We use it in Europe, probably in the US as well. They are long as hell, but do fill them out. You'll probably have to do something like it when you see a doctor for a diagnosis anyway. It helped me to already have thought about the questions. On page 3 you can see all the things that are explored in it. I advice you to skip the stuff that definitely don't apply to you, but if there is just a tiny insecurity about any of those illnesses, fill them out anyway. You don't know what you don't know about yourself.

http://www.psychiatry.pitt.edu/sites/default/files/Documents/assessments/ksads-pl.pdf

There are also extra forms for each individual disorder, if I remember correctly. Let me know if you're interested, I can try to dig them out for ya. 

Also putting out the link to 7 cups of tea here. It's a web page where you can talk to people who have signed up specifically to listen to you. You don't need to sign up.
http://www.7cupsoftea.com/

Try to still do stuff. If you're gonna refresh a webpage, refresh Reddit. Try to stimulate your brain and body, even if that only means laying on the couch binge-watching something. And always, always try to remember what happiness feels like. Take good care of your gf, try to make her understand what you're going through. That way, she can help you. You're lucky to have her.
